papers_read.title_as_printed: Multimodal ensemble model for Alzheimer's disease conversion prediction from Early Mild Cognitive Impairment subjects (Velazquez & Lee, Computers in Biology and Medicine 151 (2022) 106201)
Class activation attention transfer neural networks for MCI conversion prediction (Luo et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 156 (2023) 106700)

what_each_reports.P-1: ADNI EMCI only (383 patients: 49 converters, 335 non-converters; conversion by the diagnosis at the last exam, described as within five years). Ensemble of a random forest on nine clinical/biomarker features (age, race, APOE4, hippocampal and ventricular volume, ADAS11, ADAS13, FAQ, MMSE) and a NASNet CNN on single-slice DTI ADC images from 90 patients; exam-visit oversampling; held-out test split: accuracy 98.81%, AUC 0.992; clinical-only RF 92.86%, DTI-only CNN 96.43% (Tables 5, 6, 8). No external cohort.
what_each_reports.P-3: ADNI-1/2 all MCI (298 sMCI, 295 pMCI; pMCI = dementia within 36 months), single baseline T1 MRI only, 5-layer 3D CNN with class-activation attention transfer, 5-fold CV on Wen et al.'s splits: CAAT ensemble accuracy 74.61%, AUC 0.780, sensitivity/specificity 0.75/0.75 (Table 3). Authors note 5-fold CV was used for tuning and selection and may be optimistically biased.

quantity_a: Held-out accuracy of a clinical-feature + DTI ensemble for eventual conversion to AD (roughly 5-year horizon) among ADNI early-MCI patients.
quantity_b: 5-fold CV accuracy of a T1-MRI-only 3D CNN for conversion to dementia within 36 months among all ADNI MCI (EMCI, LMCI, MCI) patients.
incompatible_if_same: If the quantity were the same, 98.81% vs 74.61% (fold variance 0.002) could not both hold. But the population, horizon, and predictor set all differ, and neither paper states a result about the other's setting.

gates.task: match in outline (T2 MCI-to-AD conversion), but the population behind the label differs (EMCI only vs all MCI) and the horizon differs (last available exam, stated as within five years, vs 36 months).
gates.validation_tier: mismatch in form: P-1 a single random held-out split (plus unspecified cross-validation), P-3 5-fold CV on published benchmark splits; both internal only.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-1 clinical scores, APOE4 and volumetrics plus DTI; P-3 structural T1 MRI only.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible endpoint: different horizon (about 5 years vs 36 months) and different source population (EMCI vs mixed MCI). Metric type (accuracy) matches.
performance_validity: flag applies to P-1: 98.81% accuracy (AUC 0.992) on internal validation only, with the imaging arm resting on 90 patients (16 converters), exam-visit oversampling for the clinical arm, and repeated tuning ('the experiment was repeated several dozen times per model'). A performance comparison resting on P-1 cannot be genuine.
independence: Distinct author groups; both draw on ADNI MCI participants, so EMCI subjects may overlap; not determinable.
grounds: The population behind the label differs: P-1 is restricted to early MCI, P-3 pools EMCI, LMCI and MCI.
The endpoint horizon differs: P-1 uses conversion at the last exam (stated as within five years), P-3 conversion within 36 months.
The predictor set and modality differ: P-1 combines clinical scores, APOE4, volumetrics and DTI; P-3 uses one baseline T1 image only.
Independently, P-1 meets the performance-validity exclusion (98.81% on internal validation only, imaging arm N=90), so no performance contradiction resting on it could be genuine.

evidence_quotes.quote: 383 Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) patients were collected from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Within this set, 49 patients would eventually convert to AD
When both modalities (clinical data and DTI scans) are provided, our weighted ensemble model achieves an EMCI-to-AD conversion prediction accuracy of 98.81%.
These were then grouped into 90 unique EMCI patients, where 16 would convert to AD (EMCI_C) and 74 would not (EMCI_NC).
With this approach, our model achieves an accuracy of 98.8% on EMCI to AD conversion prediction within five years.
we take a single MRI image of a patient diagnosed with MCI at a given time and accurately predict whether they will be diagnosed with AD within 3 years.
At the start (baseline time), all selected subjects were diagnosed with MCI, early MCI (EMCI), or late MCI (LMCI).

record_defects: task_equivalence true / dataset_family_equivalence true treat the two as the same task; the population (EMCI vs all MCI) and horizon (about 5 years vs 36 months) differ.
registry Sample_N_Approx for P-3 is 1587, which is the source-task pool; the conversion analysis uses 593 MCI subjects.

The long bridging-evidence list consists of other papers' headline scores and does not identify a separating condition for this pair; the gap is explained by the pair's own design differences and by P-1's near-ceiling internal result.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing short of both models evaluated on the same MCI population, horizon and inputs; even then P-1's result would stay excluded by the performance-validity rule unless replicated externally.
